user.title: What would you like to track?
user.description: A monitor watches one activity rule and creates its own Home Assistant device. {monitor_examples}

data_description.monitor_type: Each choice has a short explanation. Select the one that best matches the activity you want to measure.

data.name: Name this monitor
data.active_states: States that mean the activity is happening

data_description.name: A clear name used for this monitor device and its entities, for example “Living room TV” or “Barber visits” .
data_description.entity_id: The entity whose state is observed. Activity Tracker never changes it.
data_description.active_states: Enter exact state values separated by commas, for example: on, playing, paused. Moving between these values keeps one session open.
data_description.zone_entity_id: Only this zone counts as activity. Home, away, and every other zone do not count.
data_description.person_entity_id: Used for identity and naming only. The selected presence sensor is the source of truth for activity.
data_description.area_id: Used for the area identity and name. An area alone does not report who is present.
data_description.presence_entity_id: The binary sensor that reports whether the selected person is in the selected area. It is normally active when its state is on.
data_description.value_source: Use Entity state when it is the application identifier. Use Entity attribute when the identifier is stored in an attribute.
data_description.value_attribute: Required for an attribute source. Prefer a stable identifier such as a package name when available.
data_description.label_attribute: Optional friendly name shown in Home Assistant. Changing this label does not create a different tracked application.

behavior.title: Choose session behavior
behavior.description: These choices apply only to this monitor. They determine which completed activity is retained and how short interruptions are handled.

data.unavailable_tolerance_seconds: Wait before handling an unavailable source (seconds)

data_description.duration_unit: Choose how duration sensors are shown. This affects only the display, not tracked time or history.
data_description.retention_days: Number of calendar days to keep compact daily summaries. The minimum is 7 days; older summaries are deleted during cleanup.
data_description.minimum_session_seconds: Completed sessions shorter than this many seconds are discarded. Use 0 to keep every completed session.
data_description.unavailable_behavior: Choose whether an unavailable or unknown source ends activity, remains pending briefly, or is reported as unknown time.
data_description.unavailable_tolerance_seconds: How long an unavailable source may remain pending before the selected unavailable behavior applies. Use 0 to apply it immediately.
data_description.merge_gap_seconds: For brief observed inactive gaps such as GPS noise. The gap itself is not activity. Use 0 to end the session immediately.
data_description.import_recorder_history: Rebuild retained daily summaries from the source entity's existing Recorder history. This can take a moment and starts from the configured retention period.

periods.title: Choose report periods
periods.description: Select one or more periods for report sensors. A rolling period means local calendar dates, not an exact number of 24-hour blocks.

data_description.periods: Today starts at local midnight. Current week and month follow Home Assistant's local calendar.
data_description.rolling_days: Optional positive whole-day values separated by commas, for example: 7, 30, 35. “35” means today plus the previous 34 local dates.

period_metrics.title: Choose sensors to create
period_metrics.description: Select the report sensors to create for {period}.

data.period_metrics: Reports and sensors to create for this period

data_description.period_metrics: Each selected metric creates an entity only for this report period.

metrics.title: Choose monitor-wide sensors
metrics.description: Optionally select sensors that do not use a report period.

data_description.enabled_metrics: Current, latest-session, and weekday sensors create one entity for this monitor.

review.title: Review this monitor
review.description: Create {name} using {source}. It will have {metrics} selected metric type(s) across these periods: {periods}. You can change session behavior later in Configure.

error.required: Provide at least one value before continuing.
error.invalid_rolling_days: Use only positive whole numbers separated by commas, for example: 7, 30, 35.

init.title: Edit monitor
init.description: Update the activity rule, source, reports, sensors, and session behavior. At the end, choose what to do with existing history.

data_description.monitor_type: You may change the monitor type as well as its source. Changing the rule can make existing history incomparable.

data_description.duration_unit: Choose how duration sensors are shown. This affects only the display, not tracked time or history.
data_description.retention_days: Number of calendar days to retain. A longer report period cannot be reliable if it exceeds this value.
data_description.minimum_session_seconds: Discard completed sessions shorter than this duration. Set to 0 to keep all completed sessions.
data_description.unavailable_behavior: How an unknown or unavailable source affects the in-progress session.
data_description.unavailable_tolerance_seconds: Wait this many seconds before applying the unavailable behavior.
data_description.merge_gap_seconds: Treat a brief observed inactive interval as part of one visit or use session. The gap is excluded from duration.

history.title: Choose what to do with history
history.description: Use reimport when the changed rule should be applied to the available Recorder history. It replaces summaries within the retention period.

data_description.history_action: Keep preserves current summaries; clear deletes them; reimport rebuilds them using the configured source and Recorder history.

confirm_history.title: Confirm history action
confirm_history.description: Confirm {action} before changing retained history. Clear removes all retained summaries; reimport replaces only the Recorder-backed range.

data.confirm_history_action: I understand this changes retained history

options.entity_state: Entity state — track an entity while it is in selected states.
options.zone: Person or device in a zone — track visits to one Home Assistant zone.
options.area_presence: Person in an internal area — use a presence binary sensor for one area.
options.foreground_application: Foreground application — track the app currently reported by an entity.
options.generic: Custom state rule — track any entity using selected active states.

options.state: Entity state — the application value is the entity's state.
options.attribute: Entity attribute — the application value is stored in an attribute.

options.current_day: Today — from local midnight until now.
options.current_week: Current week — using Home Assistant's local calendar.
options.current_month: Current month — using Home Assistant's local calendar.

options.last_session_start: Most recent completed session start time
options.last_session_end: Most recent completed session end time
options.days_since_last_session: Days since the most recent completed session
options.unknown_duration: Time whose activity status is unknown

options.end: End the session — stop activity when the source is unavailable.
options.pending: Keep it pending — wait for the source to return before deciding.
options.unknown: Mark the time as unknown — preserve the interval as uncertain.

options.keep: Keep existing history — use the new rule only for future activity.
options.clear: Clear existing history — start collecting again now.
options.reimport: Reimport from Recorder — rebuild retained history with the new rule.
